project.name: maxrim
project.description: MaxRIM is an AI-assisted research intelligence and management platform for healthcare researchers, providing project-scoped PDF ingestion, evidence retrieval, and citation-verified report generation in one auditable workflow. It also supports systematic-review tasks such as deduplication, AI-assisted screening, data extraction, and export. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: MaxRIM is an AI research assistant for healthcare researchers: users upload PDFs into a project, ask questions, and get cited, verified reports. README.md lays out the full target design (Docling-to-Qdrant ingestion, a Planner/Researcher/Synthesizer/Verifier loop, the API), while CLAUDE.md records how it was actually built in five steps: ingest, ask, verify, eval, API. That build order is the spine of this tour.

tour.title: Configuration and Dependencies
tour.description: Before any code, see what the project stands on. pyproject.toml declares a uv-managed Python 3.12 project pulling in Docling, FastAPI, LangGraph, OpenAI, Qdrant and SQLAlchemy, and config.py is the single pydantic-settings class that reads .env for model names, Qdrant Cloud credentials, retrieval toggles and the database URL. Nothing else reads environment variables, so every later module gets its models and feature flags from here.
tour.languageLesson: pydantic-settings maps environment variables onto typed class fields, so a missing or malformed setting fails at startup with a validation error instead of surfacing deep inside a request.

tour.title: Ingestion Pipeline
tour.description: Step 1 of the build turns a PDF into searchable vectors. ingest.py parses with Docling, embeds chunks with OpenAI plus a bm25 sparse vector, and upserts to Qdrant with uuid5 point ids derived from project, document hash and chunk index, so re-ingesting the same file creates zero new points. Its high fan-in shows how many parts of the system (API jobs, evals, tests) depend on it.

tour.title: Smart Chunking and Sections
tour.description: Ingestion quality hinges on how documents are split. chunking.py classifies each PDF as article, report or generic and regroups Docling HybridChunker pieces by section within token budgets, and sections.py makes one LLM call per document to build a repaired heading outline that assigns each chunk a canonical section. The design spec explains the reasoning; per CLAUDE.md these changes moved the eval baseline to recall 1.00 / MRR 0.86.

tour.title: Retrieval and Answering
tour.description: Step 2 queries what Step 3 stored. ask.py runs a project-filtered Qdrant search (dense, or hybrid bm25 plus reciprocal rank fusion), optionally reranks, and asks the LLM for an answer that cites chunk ids, removing any invented citation. papers.py adds a paper resolver that routes a question to the specific project papers it names, declining papers the project lacks.
tour.languageLesson: Reciprocal rank fusion merges two ranked lists by summing 1/(k + rank) per item, so a document that ranks well in either keyword or vector search rises without needing comparable raw scores.

tour.title: Verified Research Loop
tour.description: Step 3 wraps retrieval in a plan, gather, synthesize, verify loop. research.py plans sub-questions, collects evidence, synthesizes a cited answer and has a guard model verify each claim, failing closed and retrying on unsupported or invented claims. rails.py adds input and output guardrails, and web.py and pubmed.py contribute extra evidence that is explicitly marked as untrusted.

tour.title: Offline Evaluation
tour.description: Step 4 makes every change measurable. evaluate.py scores retrieval recall@k and MRR plus the verifier false-claim catch rate against eval/gold.json, a set of gold questions across six healthcare papers. CLAUDE.md requires running it before and after any change to chunking, retrieval, prompts or models, which is how the chunking and hybrid-search decisions in Steps 4 and 5 were made.

tour.title: Data Model and Auth
tour.description: Step 5 starts with persistence. db.py is the SQLAlchemy schema for users, projects, documents, conversations, research runs, references, papers, screening decisions and extraction columns, and it is the most depended-on file in the graph. auth.py adds stdlib scrypt password hashing and HS256 JWTs, which the API uses to tie every project to its owner.

tour.title: FastAPI Application
tour.description: app.py is the runtime entry point (uvicorn app:create_app --factory) and the root of the code dependency graph: it imports almost every module seen so far. It wires auth, projects, document upload, research runs, conversations, the screening assistant and the screening funnel into one API, building the project_id filter server-side so clients can never query another project. The API design spec documents how these endpoints wrap Steps 1 to 4.
tour.languageLesson: An app factory (create_app) builds a fresh FastAPI instance per call, which lets tests inject fake settings, clients and executors instead of relying on module-level globals.

tour.title: Background Jobs
tour.description: Ingestion and research are too slow and too fragile to run inside a request. jobs.py runs Docling ingestion in a one-worker child process so a native crash fails one document rather than the server, and also runs research, paper resolution and confirmed screening or extraction work. It enforces the rule that a document is never marked ready before its Qdrant upsert succeeded.

tour.title: Systematic Review Funnel
tour.description: The newest subsystem supports systematic reviews end to end. references.py parses PubMed, BibTeX, RIS and Scopus/Web of Science exports, dedup.py groups records into papers via union-find on DOI, PMID and normalized title, screening.py issues quoted AI title/abstract verdicts against criteria, and funnel.py is the database service layer that ties them together. The design spec explains the full flow from import to screening.

tour.title: Full Text and Extraction
tour.description: After screening, included papers need their data pulled out. fulltext.py finds legally free PDFs via Europe PMC and Unpaywall with SSRF-safe downloads, extraction.py asks the model for one value per paper backed by a verbatim quote, and outputs.py and answers.py export results as CSV, Excel or Word while neutralizing spreadsheet formula injection.

tour.title: LangGraph Screening Assistant
tour.description: agent.py is the conversational layer over the funnel: a LangGraph assistant that guards input and lets the model call in-process tools for status, criteria, papers, columns, exports and web, PubMed or research searches. It reuses the guardrails from Step 6 and the funnel services from Steps 11 and 12, so the chat is a thin, project-scoped interface rather than new logic.

tour.title: Web UI
tour.description: The static single-page UI is served by app.py at the root path. index.html is the shell, app.js handles auth, projects, PDF uploads, conversations and cited answer cards over the /api/v1 endpoints, and screening.js renders the funnel views: criteria cards, paper tables, review queue, blind labelling and exports.

tour.title: Tests and End-to-End Evals
tour.description: Quality is guarded at two levels. tests/conftest.py supplies fake settings, a fake OpenAI client and an inline executor so unit tests never touch the network, while evals/run.py runs golden questions through the live API with DeepEval judging and evals/compare.py gates a candidate against the promoted baseline (PASS, FAIL or REVIEW). RESULTS.md logs every run, making it the project history of what each change actually did.
